method: Source found by search and checked on the AUT institutional repository record (title, authors, journal, year, volume, pages, DOI, design, size, findings).

claims.claim: مراجعة علمية لتسع وأربعين تجربة وجدت أن الفائدة تتوقف تقريبًا عند 1.6 غرام لكل كيلوغرام من وزنك يوميًا.
claims.source_title: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength in healthy adults
claims.authors: Morton RW, Murphy KT, McKellar SR, Schoenfeld BJ, Henselmans M, Helms E, Aragon AA, Devries MC, Banfield L, Krieger JW, Phillips SM
claims.study_type: Systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of randomized controlled trials
claims.population: Healthy adults doing resistance training for at least 6 weeks
claims.main_finding: Protein supplementation increased resistance-training gains in fat-free mass (0.30 kg) and strength; beyond a total protein intake of about 1.62 g/kg/day, no further fat-free mass gains were seen.
claims.limitations: Effects are modest; the breakpoint refers to total daily protein, not supplement dose; age and training-status effects come from meta-regression across trials.

claims.claim: فوق هذا الرقم لم تظهر فائدة إضافية للعضل.
claims.main_finding: No further fat-free mass gains above about 1.62 g/kg/day of total protein.

claims.claim: شخص وزنه 70 كيلوغرامًا يحتاج نحو 112 غرامًا يوميًا.
claims.main_finding: 1.6 g/kg/day for a 70 kg person is about 112 g of protein a day.
claims.limitations: An example for healthy adults; people with kidney disease should ask their doctor (stated in the caption).

claims.claim: المهم مجموع البروتين في يومك، من الطعام أو المكملات، مع تمارين المقاومة.
claims.main_finding: The breakpoint applies to total daily protein intake; supplements helped only as a way of raising total intake, alongside resistance training.
claims.limitations: Does not compare protein sources directly.
